content.text: The files are named `main_p1.png` through `main_p15.png`. Let me read the first 8 pages.

Here is the page-by-page visual inspection report:

**Page 1 (main_p1.png):** Title page. Title is "Death Avoidance as the Dominant Routing Signal: A Counterfactual Analysis on ScienceWorld." Anonymous ACL submission. Contains the Abstract (left column) and the beginning of Section 1 Introduction (right column). Two-column ACL format with line numbers visible. No figures or tables. Text is legible, margins look correct, font sizes are standard. This is main text.

**Page 2 (main_p2.png):** Continuation of Section 1 Introduction (contributions list) and beginning of Section 2 Problem Setup. Two-column text, line numbers present. No figures or tables. Text is clean and legible. Margins are fine. Main text.

**Page 3 (main_p3.png):** Section 2 continues (2.2 Counterfactual Episode Collection, 2.3 Episode-Level Labeling). Contains **Figure 1** in the right column -- a flowchart showing the counterfactual episode collection and analysis pipeline. The figure is legible but somewhat small; the text within the flowchart boxes is readable but tight. The figure placement is reasonable (top of right column). Several equations are present (Eq. 1, 2). Main text.

**Page 4 (main_p4.png):** Contains **Algorithm 1** (Episode-Level Counterfactual Labeling) spanning the top of the left column. Sections 2.4 Death Avoidance Factor and the beginning of Section 3 Experiments. Dense text with equations (Eq. 3, 4, 5). The algorithm box is well-formatted and legible. No visual issues. Main text.

**Page 5 (main_p5.png):** Contains **Figure 2** (a scatter plot, left column) and **Table 1** (right column, showing death rates under agent improvement methods). Section 3.1 Death Decomposition continues, and Section 3.2 Multi-Model Validation begins. Figure 2 is legible with data points, regression line, and p-values clearly shown. Table 1 is clean with clear column headers. No overlapping or cut-off elements. Main text.

**Page 6 (main_p6.png):** Contains **Table 2** (cross-environment label distribution, right column top) and **Table 3** (episode-weighted mean scores on ScienceWorld, right column middle). Sections 3.4 (Cross-Domain Negative Contrast: MATH), 3.5 (Cross-Environment Contrasts), 3.6 (Baselines), and 3.7 (Router Training as Diagnostic Probe). Tables are legible and well-placed. The page is dense but readable. Main text.

**Page 7 (main_p7.png):** Section 4 Related Work and Section 5 Discussion begin. No figures or tables. Two-column dense text. The Related Work section covers Tool Use and External Computation, Adaptive Computation and Routing, LLM Agent Environments and Reasoning, and Safe RL. Text is legible and well-formatted. Main text.

**Page 8 (main_p8.png):** Section 5 Discussion continues (covering non-triviality of death dominance, DAF and framework applicability). Section 6 Conclusion appears. The **Limitations** section begins at the bottom of the page. No figures or tables. Text is legible. This is the final page of main text content -- the Conclusion and Limitations section are both on this page.

**Summary findings:**

- **Main text boundary:** The main text (Sections 1-6 plus Limitations) ends on page 8. This fits within the ACL 8-page main text limit. References and appendices presumably start on page 9 onward (the paper has 15 pages total).
- **Visual formatting problems:** No significant visual issues detected across pages 1-8. No overlapping text, no cut-off figures, no margin violations, no font size problems. All figures (Figure 1, Figure 2) and tables (Tables 1, 2, 3) are legible and properly placed.
- **Line numbers** are present throughout (appropriate for review submission).
- **Minor observation:** Figure 1 (page 3) is somewhat small and the text within the flowchart boxes, while readable, could benefit from slightly larger font. This is a minor concern and not a formatting violation.
- **Density:** Pages 6 and 7 are quite dense with text. Page 6 packs two tables and four subsections, which is efficient but tight.
